title: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions and Mixed Numerals
seo_title: Year 7 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Fractions of Amounts, Reciprocals and Division (Free, Answer Key)

meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing fractions for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7N06): fractions of amounts, multiplying fractions and mixed numerals, reciprocals, dividing fractions and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Multiply: tops × tops, bottoms × bottoms. Divide: multiply by the reciprocal.
key_sub: Change mixed numerals to improper fractions first, and simplify your answer.
body_html:
How it works

Multiplying: multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators, then simplify. “Of” means multiply: 2/3 of 12 = 2/3 × 12 = 8.

Dividing: keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction (use its reciprocal).

Change mixed numerals into improper fractions before you multiply or divide.

Example

Work out 3/4 × 2/5.

3 × 2 = 6 and 4 × 5 = 20.

6/20 simplifies to 3/10.

Answer: 3/10

Example

Work out 2/3 ÷ 4/9.

Keep, change, flip: 2/3 × 9/4.

= 18/12 = 3/2.

Answer: 1 1/2

Example

Work out 1 1/2 × 2 2/3.

Improper: 3/2 × 8/3 = 24/6.

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying the denominator by a whole number: 2/5 × 3 = 6/5, not 6/15.
  • Flipping the first fraction instead of the second when dividing.
  • Multiplying mixed numerals in parts: 1 1/2 × 2 2/3 is not 2 2/6.
  • Thinking the answer to a division must be smaller: 6 ÷ 3/4 = 8.

faq.a: Multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, then simplify. You do not need a common denominator.
Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction. 2/3 ÷ 4/9 = 2/3 × 9/4 = 3/2.
The number you multiply by to get 1. The reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3, and the reciprocal of 4 is 1/4.

faq.q: Why can dividing by a fraction give a bigger answer?
faq.a: Because you are asking how many small pieces fit in. 6 ÷ 3/4 = 8 pieces of three quarters.

items.q: A paddock is 45 of a farm. 23 of the paddock is planted with wheat. What fraction of the farm is wheat?
items.e: “Of” means multiply: 45 × 23 = 815.

items.q: 35 of a class are girls. 12 of the girls play netball. What fraction of the class are girls who play netball?
items.e: “Of” means multiply: 35 × 12 = 310.

items.q: A bottle is 78 full of sunscreen. 27 of the sunscreen is used at the beach. What fraction of the bottle was used?

items.q: A rectangle measures 3 12 m by 1 13 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 3 12 × 1 13 = 72 × 43 = 4 23 m².

items.q: A rectangle measures 1 14 m by 23 m. What is its area?

items.q: A rectangle measures 2 14 m by 2 23 m. What is its area?

items.q: A bottle holds 34 of a litre. How many bottles can be filled from 15 litres?
items.e: 15 ÷ 34 = 15 × 43 = 20.

items.q: A swimming lesson lasts 13 of an hour. How many lessons fit into 4 hours?
items.e: 4 ÷ 13 = 4 × 31 = 12.

items.q: Each scoop holds 56 of a cup. How many scoops are in 3 13 cups of flour?
items.e: 3 13 ÷ 56 = 103 × 65 = 4.

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 2 13 cups of milk. How much milk is needed for 2 people?
items.e: Half of 2 13 = 73 × 12 = 1 16 cups.

items.q: 35 of a pavlova is left. It is shared equally between 6 people. What fraction of the whole pavlova does each person get?
items.e: 35 ÷ 6 = 35 × 16 = 110.

items.q: 34 of a pizza is shared equally between 4 friends. What fraction of the pizza does each friend get?
items.e: 34 ÷ 4 = 34 × 14 = 316.
